title: The Twelve are refilled and sent across the sea
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Far West, Missouri, on 8 July 1838. Leaders had prayed to know the Lord’s will about the Twelve. Dissent in 1837 and 1838 had cost the quorum four members. Luke Johnson, John Boynton, and Lyman Johnson were cut off, and William McLellin was found in transgression. Thomas Marsh, the quorum president, was the only apostle at the meeting.
summary: The revelation calls for a conference to organize the Twelve and fill the places of the fallen. It tells Thomas to stay in Zion for a time to publish the word. The other apostles are to keep preaching with humility and patience. If they do, the Lord promises to provide for their families. Next spring they are to cross “the great waters” to preach. They are to leave from the Far West temple site on 26 April 1839. John Taylor, John Page, Wilford Woodruff, and Willard Richards are named to fill the vacancies.

contextNote.title: A departure fixed to a date and a place
contextNote.text: The quorum had lost members and needed both new apostles and a mission. Verse 5 sets an exact date and place for leaving: 26 April 1839, at the Far West temple site. Verse 4 gives the purpose, to preach the gospel over the great waters. By that spring the Saints had been driven from Missouri, and Far West was hostile ground. Wilford Woodruff’s journal records a meeting at the site that day, where new apostles were ordained. In this passage, the date ties the mission’s start to the place where the temple was to stand.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 115–120 covers this call to the Twelve. What promise does verse 3 attach to serving “in all lowliness of heart,” and who receives it?

newPeople.name: John E. Page
newPeople.why: named in v. 6; called to fill a vacancy in the Quorum of the Twelve in 1838

reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Far West, 8 July 1838, answering a prayer about the Twelve. JSP historical introduction read for the four fallen apostles, those present (Marsh the only apostle), and the 26 April 1839 meeting recorded in Woodruff's journal. Thomas in v. 2 is Thomas B. Marsh. The detail that the 26 April 1839 meeting happened at the temple site despite the expulsion is general history consistent with JSP. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
